obtained.how: the report's PDF as posted on the Forest Ecosystem Monitoring Cooperative's project page (University of Vermont), the URL in the ledger entry

bibliography.checked_against: the title page (p. 1) and the report's own suggested citation (p. 2)
bibliography.note: Suggested citation: 'Kuehne C, Puhlick JJ, and Weiskittel AR 2018. Ecological reserves in Maine: Initial results of long-term monitoring. General Technical Report. 62 p.' No publisher is named; funded by The Nature Conservancy.

claims.claim: ecological reserves carry 28.5 m²/ha of basal area in trees ≥ 12.7 cm (28.0 on non-harvested plots), against 17.4 on managed FIA plots
claims.location: p. 16, Results (live tree basal area); trees ≥ 5.0 in dbh, p. 7 and p. 9
claims.quote: Average live tree basal area was significantly lower for FIA subplots (76 ft2 ac-1)
claims.conditions: plot means (not medians): Ecological Reserve plots of inventory round 2 (2011–17; 547 remeasured plots in 20 reserves) 124 ft² ac⁻¹, non-harvested round-2 plots 122, FIA subplots on managed (non-reserve) Maine forest land 76 (10,503 subplots, most recent of the inventories spanning 2000–15); trees ≥ 5.0 in (12.7 cm) dbh on 24-ft-radius plots
claims.note: 1 ft² ac⁻¹ = 0.22957 m² ha⁻¹: 124 → 28.47, 122 → 28.01, 76 → 17.45 (17.4 rounds down from 17.447). 'Statewide' fits the FIA comparison; the reserves are 20 sites, not a statewide sample.

claims.claim: snags ≥ 12.7 cm: 54/ha on managed FIA plots, 99 in ecological reserves, 104 on non-harvested reserve plots
claims.quote: lower on FIA subplots (22 ac-1) compared to ERM2 plots (40 ac-1
claims.conditions: mean standing dead trees ≥ 5.0 in dbh and ≥ 4.5 ft tall per acre: FIA 22, round-2 reserves 40, non-harvested round-2 42

claims.claim: large snags ≥ 40 cm: 1.7/ha managed, 3.3 reserves, 12.3 Big Reed old growth
claims.location: p. 20, Results (large standing dead TPA); Big Reed, p. 28
claims.quote: standing dead TPA was significantly lower on FIA subplots (0.70 ac-1)
claims.conditions: large = dbh ≥ 15.8 in (40.1 cm): FIA 0.70, round-2 reserves 1.33, non-harvested round-2 0.99 per acre; Big Reed Forest Reserve 4.97 per acre from 25 plots measured once (not in the statistical analyses because not yet remeasured)
claims.note: × 2.471: 1.73, 3.29, 12.28 per ha. The non-harvested reserve value the table leaves blank is 0.99/acre = 2.4/ha (lower than all reserve plots).

claims.claim: downed coarse woody debris 39 m³/ha managed, 45 reserves, 49.5 non-harvested reserve plots, 82 Big Reed old growth
claims.location: p. 20, Results (total downed woody debris); Big Reed, p. 28
claims.quote: Total downed woody debris volume on FIA subplots (557 ft3 ac-1) was significantly lower
claims.conditions: pieces ≥ 3 in (7.6 cm) diameter at the transect intersection (decay class 5 ≥ 5 in), line-intersect transects, volume by Woodall & Monleon 2008 eq. 2: FIA 557, round-2 reserves 644, non-harvested 708 ft³ ac⁻¹; Big Reed 1166 ft³ ac⁻¹

claims.claim: large CWD ≥ 40 cm: 1.8 m³/ha managed, 4.9 reserves
claims.quote: Large (diameter ≥ 15.75 in) downed woody debris volume on FIA subplots (26 ft3 ac-1)
claims.conditions: diameter at transect intersect ≥ 15.75 in (40.0 cm): FIA 26, round-2 reserves 70, non-harvested 75 ft³ ac⁻¹
claims.note: × 0.069973: 1.82 and 4.90 m³/ha (non-harvested 5.2, left blank in the table).

claims.claim: managed forest carries about half the snags of the ecological reserves and about half the downed wood of old growth
claims.location: p. 16 and p. 20 (FIA vs reserves); p. 28 (Big Reed)
claims.quote: total downed woody debris volume (1166 ft3 ac-1) were all considerably higher on Big Reed
claims.conditions: snags 22 vs 40 per acre (0.55); downed wood 557 vs 1166 ft³ ac⁻¹ (0.48)
claims.note: Both ratios hold. Against the reserves (not old growth) managed forest has 87 % of the downed wood (557/644).

notes: Every number the paper takes is a metric conversion of the report's imperial means, and all convert correctly. Other values: very large live trees (dbh ≥ 20.1 in) 1.43/acre on FIA vs 2.69 on round-2 reserves and 4.48 at Big Reed; large live trees (≥ 15.8 in) 5.7 vs 14.7/acre; gross growth 69 vs 75 ft³ ac⁻¹ yr⁻¹; mortality 18 vs 32 ft³ ac⁻¹ yr⁻¹ (pp. 16–20). Spruce–fir plots had more basal area and snags than maple–beech–birch; maple–beech–birch had about twice the very large trees. The reserves were partly logged before designation and are still gaining volume.
